When sulfur-containing compounds react with oxidizing acids, they often produce toxic gases like hydrogen sulfide (H2S) or sulfur dioxide (SO2).

Oxidizing acids (like nitric acid, perchloric acid, etc.) can oxidize the sulfur in dithiocarbamates, potentially leading to the formation of toxic sulfur-containing gases. This is a common hazard with many sulfur compounds.
